title: Mortgage redemption disputes - the borrower's legal rights
p1: Many borrowers believe that once a mortgage is created, the lender holds all the power. But the law often gives borrowers a right that can change the entire dispute: the right to redeem their property.
p2: A common misconception is that missing payments permanently ends a borrower's claim over the property. In reality, redemption means the borrower can seek release of the mortgage by clearing the lawful dues, subject to applicable legal conditions.
p3: The surprising part? A lender's security interest does not always mean ownership. The mortgage exists to secure repayment, not to automatically transfer the property. Borrowers may have remedies if a lender refuses redemption, demands unlawful amounts, or ignores settlement obligations. Knowing these rights can prevent unnecessary loss of valuable assets.
conclusion: Have you seen cases where borrowers lost property because they were unaware of their right to redeem a mortgage? What safeguards should borrowers know before signing loan agreements?
